extracted.intended_audience: Commissioner of Indian Affairs; Department of the Interior officials and Indian agency administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Operational and policy standards for management of Indian reservations and agency schools (education, land allotment, policing, health, and vocational training) as expressed in an 1880 United States Indian Agent annual report for Washington Territory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boarding-school capacity and provisioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Additions should be made to the boarding-school buildings, both at Puyallup and Chehalis Reservations, so as to accommodate at least 100 pupils at the former and at least 50 at the latter reservation school.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide funds sufficient to feed, clothe, lodge, and employ additional instructors for that number of pupils, and funds for construction of additional buildings. The report ties school capacity to the ability to obtain pupils (food/clothing/boarding being limiting factors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory industrial boarding education for children
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision should be at once made by government for placing all Indian children between five and eighteen years of age in industrial boarding schools, nolens volens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recommendation frames compulsory enrollment as a policy tool to replace 'ignorant' customs with training in English and practical arts; implementation implies establishing enough boarding-school spaces and resources for all children in this age range.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditional fee-simple land titles (allotment policy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Give Indians fee-simple titles to portions of lands on their reservations under proper restrictions as to permanent settlement, improvement, buildings, etc., and inalienable for, say, ten years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No title should be given until the Indian has settled upon and improved the land to a specified extent and given evidence of subsisting himself and family by cultivation. Aim is to encourage permanent settlement and productive improvement before conveyance; treats inalienability period (~10 years) as a safeguard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enfranchisement upon qualification
rubrics_metrics.description: Government should at once make provision for enfranchising Indians, when they have become properly qualified, with all the rights and privileges of citizens, as fully as said rights are bestowed on foreigners who come to our country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enfranchisement is to be contingent on meeting stated qualifications (not fully enumerated here) and is presented as an incentive to prepare for citizenship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of state/territorial law
rubrics_metrics.description: All Indians should be amenable to the laws of the State or Territory in which they reside, except as to taxation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy recommendation to place Indians under local civil/criminal law jurisdiction (with the stated tax exception); implies harmonizing reservation governance with territorial/state legal frameworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational pedagogy: thorough mastery before advancement
rubrics_metrics.description: Pupils should review each book thoroughly so as to read it all fluently before advancing to another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents superficial appearances of progress; the agent endorses mastery-based progression (reading, arithmetic, writing). Example: primer→first reader→second reader with full review at each stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combined academic and industrial/vocational curriculum
rubrics_metrics.description: A good common-school English education should be given together with practical knowledge and training in necessary farming, domestic, and mechanical industries and arts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: School programs should teach reading, writing, arithmetic, music, and also farming, carpentry, blacksmithing, cooking, washing, garment-making, and other domestic/mechanical skills; industrial teacher and apprentices to conduct farm and trade instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: School scheduling and extracurricular practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Schools should include regular practice in vocal music (twice daily) and a weekly singing-school exercise; Sunday school and Bible classes are also part of routine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Daily practice and set weekly devotional/singing times are cited as components of the institution's regimen; religious instruction and music are presented as important for character and discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: School siting to minimize negative local influences
rubrics_metrics.description: School location should be changed away from principal Indian towns so scholars are kept from constant association with older Indians whose influences hinder progress (example: relocate to south side of Point Greenville).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Siting schools at some distance from native population centers is recommended to reduce exposure to 'heathen customs and practices' and to increase effectiveness of civilizing/educational efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident government employes and on-site administration
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence of government agents and employes living among tribes is necessary to prevent moral and physical deterioration and to maintain steady improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detached reservations without resident agents/employes surrounded by white settlements tend to decay; agents should reside nearby and supervise schooling, police, and industrial efforts to sustain progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local justice procedures and appellate oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Criminal cases on reservation are to be tried by the chief of police; civil cases (debt, trespass, domestic trouble, etc.) are to be tried by the council—with the right of appeal from both courts to the agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish clear division: police handle crimes, tribal council handles civil disputes, agent retains appellate review. This procedural arrangement is recommended and described as in effect on Puyallup Reservation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indian police organization and deployment
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorize and appoint Indian police for reservations; they should keep order and take pride in their duties; small detached police (sheriffs) can serve individual villages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A force of Indian policemen is presented as economical and effective; at some agencies police reside at separate villages and act as local peace officers/sheriffs with supervisory duties. Proper nomination/organization is necessary for full effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical staffing and infrastructure (hospital necessity)
rubrics_metrics.description: A resident physician and proper hospital facilities on the reservation are needed to maintain sanitary condition and deliver effective treatment; lack of nursing/hospital care undermines confidence in modern medicine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physician success is limited without proper nursing and a hospital; trivial reporting by physicians should be tempered, but central recommendation is to provide a hospital so treatment and outcomes improve and Indians trust medical care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship and trade training programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Young men should be trained in trades (carpenter, blacksmith, farmer) and apprenticeships to produce skillful and useful labor comparable to white counterparts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carpentry and furniture-making projects, and trade apprenticeships under a skilled instructor, are concrete examples; trade training supports self-sufficiency and employment opportunities (including work for nearby white farms and mills).

rubrics_metrics.name: Parental/community support for day schools
rubrics_metrics.description: For day schools, parents are expected to furnish food and clothing for children; Indians offered to provide materials for buildings if government supplies teachers and erects structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy implementation can leverage community willingness to contribute material resources, while government funds teachers and construction; parental support and local contribution are factors in sustaining day schools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition and fulfillment of treaty-based patents and titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant patents/titles to Indians who have adopted white customs and settled in severalty as guaranteed by treaty (twenty-year treaty period expired), to remove uncertainty and encourage further improvements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issuing patents is framed as essential to encourage investment in homes/land improvements; delays or proposals to remove/ consolidate tribes elsewhere undermine incentives and should be avoided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring attendance, yields, and economic progress
rubrics_metrics.description: Track average school attendance, acreage under cultivation, crop yields, livestock counts, and fencing as measures of progress; use statistics to inform agency decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report includes detailed counts (attendance numbers, bushels of wheat/oats/potatoes, head of livestock, fencing rods made) and recommends fuller visitation and clerical support to produce accurate statistics for each tribe/band.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanitation, housing, and domestic comfort as public-health measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Promote comfortable domestic arrangements (houses with stoves, clean floors, papered walls, bedding, furniture) to reduce mortality and improve health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agent correlates improved household amenities and cleanliness with a marked decrease in mortality; resident physician and better household standards jointly contribute to public-health improvements.
